context:
Add detection after the root-cause fix, not before. Start with a small
regression test that proves external-root runs leave the worktree clean.
Then add a UAT hygiene check that snapshots the worktree-local
`benchmark_runs` path before a run and compares after each run or at teardown.
Document the invariant and wire enforcement only where an external root is
configured, so default local usage remains compatible.
description:
After `benchmark-runs-output-root-propagation` fixes the lifecycle bug,
BenchBox needs regression guardrails so long UAT and corpus runs cannot
silently fill pool worktrees with duplicate generated data again.

The 2026-06-01 evidence showed the problematic shape clearly:

- The corpus was launched from `/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.pool-01` with
  `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Despite that, `/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox.pool-01/benchmark_runs`
  accumulated about 4.2G of generated artifacts, mostly `datagen/`.
- A similar stale/generated tree already existed in the primary clone under
  `/Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox/benchmark_runs`.

This TODO adds test and operational guardrails that treat unexpected
worktree-local `benchmark_runs` writes as a failure when an external output
root is configured. The guardrails must be precise enough to avoid breaking
ordinary ad hoc runs that intentionally use the cwd-local default.

anti_patterns.why: detection and reporting come first; cleanup is handled separately.
BenchBox still supports cwd-local output for explicit local/default runs.

anti_patterns.dont: make a broad disk scan mandatory for every unit test
anti_patterns.why: keep expensive size checks in UAT/preflight paths.
add executable checks that fail when the invariant is broken.

preserves.behavior: Guardrail failures are actionable: they print the unexpected local path and expected configured root.
Long-running UAT continues to use `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR=~/Developer/benchmark_runs` as the canonical shared root.
No guardrail deletes or moves generated data automatically.
Ordinary ad hoc runs with no `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR` and no explicit `--output` can still use cwd-local `benchmark_runs`.

prior_art.concept: docs/operations/uat-framework.md:Long-Running UAT — extend the existing shared-root requirement instead of adding a competing run-root policy
make agent-write-preflight and make pr-preflight — reuse existing guard-command flow for repository hygiene checks
tests/uat/runner.py — extend the runner that already sets `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR` and passes `--output`

verifications.expected: test fails on unexpected cwd/benchmark_runs writes and passes when no local artifacts are created

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/test_runner_helpers.py tests/unit/cli/test_orchestrator_data_sharing.py tests/unit/utils/test_path_utils.py -q

work_units.notes:
When `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR` or UAT `--output` points outside the current
worktree, capture the initial state of `cwd/benchmark_runs` and fail the
run if new files or size growth appear there. The failure message must
name both the expected root and the unexpected local path.

compact audit commands for `du`, recent writes, and large-file summaries.

work_units.notes:

`benchmark_runs/`. If adding to `make pr-preflight`, gate only unexpected
growth or explicit external-root scenarios so developers can still run
small local ad hoc benchmarks.
